changes: Inline tool_call markers attached to prose are recognized as noncanonical attempts, hidden in streaming/history view and sent to bounded model repair. Stored raw text is retained.
Function-style run_command(...) and suc_action(...) are never interpreted or executed. Only a strict canonical action from a later model response may execute.
Fourth consecutive identical operation is blocked after three equal terminal outcomes; job IDs/timings/control waits excluded from comparison. Job observations and cancellation remain exempt.
Original two-attempt/action-budget limits, approvals, Stop, queued steering and context protection retained.

limits: Only synthetic localhost services and temporary-workspace commands were used. No commands, provider actions or binaries from the inspected live session were executed or modified.
Repair depends on the model emitting valid canonical JSON within the existing limits; unsupported positional syntax is not translated or guessed.

Loop detection is a conservative exact-operation/result heuristic, not semantic progress measurement or proof that repeated commands have no side effects. Changed arguments/results and intervening different actions do not trigger it.
For intentional long identical repetitions, use a single explicitly requested loop/report command or request another user turn. Active-turn steering does not reset the guard or action budget.
No installed-app GUI or live-model compatibility qualification; Universal compilation and Intel/native M1 fixture regressions are the verified scope. No new GPU/KL or performance claims.

changes: FIFO user updates enter at safe boundaries, without cancelling or modifying the active decoder.
An unexecuted proposal is retained as superseded_action; its model context explicitly says it was not executed.
A pending approval is withdrawn with a negative resolution, never granted automatically. Any revised action retains its normal approval.
Completed tool result and pending correction are separate user-role messages in the next request; one generation per session.
Corrections preserve original action/repair/subtask limits, loaded explicit instructions, drafts, attachment identity and prompt hooks.
Insufficient context or oversized wire body preserves completed tool results; pending updates remain queued.
